Article Title: India Inc ratio of upgrades to downgrades at a decade high as corporates cut borrowings
Article Text:
Indian corporations are showing resilience with a robust credit ratio of 3.2x, as reported by ICRA.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mumbai: Despite the triple shock of below normal monsoon, West Asia conflict pushing up crude and commodity prices and US tariff hurting Indian exports India inc is doing well with the ratio of upgrdes to down grade at a decadal high of 3.2x. According to rating agency ICRA the sound fianncail position of the corporartes is due to extended deleveraging by businesses and bank non-performing assets being at an all time low.ICRA said credit quality remained strong in H1 FY27, with the credit ratio rising to 3.2x from 2.8x a year earlier and 3.1x in FY26, well above the 10-year average of 1.5x. The annualised upgrade rate moderated to 14% from 17%, but downgrades fell to a multi-year low of 4%; defaults stood at 0.04%, with no investment-grade defaults.“Indian corporates enter H2 FY2027 from a position of strength, supported by healthy balance sheets and substantial liquidity buffers,” said K Ravichandran, executive vice-president and chief rating officer, ICRA. He flagged elevated crude prices, deficient monsoon, inflation and US tariff uncertainty as risks, but said strong balance sheets should prevent broad-based credit stress.Power, real estate, auto components, finance and capital goods, together about half of ICRA’s rated portfolio, contributed around 50% of upgrades.Upgrades mainly reflected stronger businesses and parents, lower project risks, higher scale, improved asset quality and deleveraging.ICRA expects crude prices, a 12% monsoon deficit and weaker reservoir levels to weigh on consumption and agricultural growth. It sees agricultural GVA growth slowing to 1% in FY27 from 3.3%, while retail inflation may average 5% against 2.1% in FY26.GDP growth is expected to moderate to 7.1% from 7.8% in Q1. Rural-linked and discretionary sectors may slow, while microfinance collections, vehicle-finance AUM growth and fleet-operator asset quality could weaken.ICRA expects any stress to remain granular, supported by healthy corporate balance sheets, bank asset quality and capitalisation. US tariff uncertainty remains an additional risk, particularly for exporters and generic pharmaceuticals.Corporate leverage is at a decade-low 2.0x, with cash covering nearly half of total debt. Policy support, public investment and spending on infrastructure and clean energy should provide further buffers against external shocks.
Article Summary: ICRA said credit quality remained strong in H1 FY27, with the credit ratio rising to 3.2x. The annualised upgrade rate moderated to 14% from 17%, but downgrades fell to a multi-year low of 4%; defaults stood at 0.04%.

Article Title: Delhi riots case: High court rejects bail pleas Of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
Article Text:
Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam denied bail by high court

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court refuses to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots.

Article Title: NEET-UG to shift online? Centre works on nationwide CBT infrastructure strategy
Article Text:
NEET-UG may shift online as Centre develops nationwide CBT infrastructure strategy

NEW DELHI: The ministry of education is developing a nationwide Computer-Based Testing (CBT) infrastructure strategy to enable the transition of NEET from its current pen-and-paper format to an online examination, officials said.While NEET has so far been conducted in pen-and-paper mode, the National Testing Agency (NTA) conducts several other examinations, including JEE-Main, Common University Entrance Test (CUET)-UG and PG, UGC-NET and CSIR UGC-NET, in computer-based mode.Once the infrastructure strategy is in place, the plan is to shift all entrance examinations to the online mode."A national examination-grade Computer-Based Testing infrastructure strategy is being formulated to close the geographic gap in test-centre availability, standardise centre-level examination-grade specifications and to permit the migration to CBT from the pen-and-paper mode examinations. The strategy is under active consideration based on a multi-model sourcing architecture," a senior Ministry of Education official was quoted as saying by PTI.The move comes amid an ongoing overhaul of the National Testing Agency (NTA), the nodal autonomous body responsible for conducting NEET-UG and other entrance examinations for higher educational institutions."The possible migration of NEET (UG) from the pen-and-paper mode to CBT, including the design of the transition, the sequencing, the infrastructure prerequisites, and the equity implications for rural, women and low-connectivity-district candidates, is being worked upon.However, the recommendations of the High-Level Task Force on exam reforms in structured consultation and concurrence of the Health Ministry and National Medical Commission, are awaited," the official said.Following the NEET paper leak earlier this year, the Centre announced that the medical entrance examination would be conducted in Computer-Based Test (CBT) mode from next year.Officials aware of the development said the plan is under active consideration, but a final decision will be taken only after the report of the Nandan Nilekani-led task force set up to overhaul India’s public examination system is received.The leak of the NEET-UG medical entrance examination paper earlier this year triggered nationwide student protests and led to the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.A day after Pradhan’s resignation, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the formation of a high-powered task force headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani to recommend reforms aimed at making the examination system leakproof.The panel has yet to submit its report.The National Eligibility Entrance Test (NEET)-UG is the country’s largest undergraduate entrance examination, with nearly 25 lakh candidates appearing for the crucial test.The National Testing Agency (NTA) conducts NEET every year for admission to medical colleges. A total of 1,08,000 seats are available for the MBBS course, of which approximately 56,000 are in government hospitals and about 52,000 in private colleges. NEET results are also used for admissions to undergraduate courses in Dentistry, Ayurveda, Unani and Siddha.
Article Summary: The ministry of education is developing a nationwide Computer-Based Testing (CBT) infrastructure strategy. Once the infrastructure strategy is in place, the plan is to shift all entrance examinations to the online mode. The move comes amid an ongoing overhaul of the National Testing Agency (NTA)

Article Title: As US cozies up to Pakistan, India warns it could impact ties
Article Text:
India and the US had in Feb announced the finalisation of the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement. However, changes in the US tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.

S Jaishankar: Delay in reaching trade deal created bumps in relationship

NEW YORK/ NEW DELHI: Amid growing US-Pakistan bonhomie, external affairs minister S Jaishankar warned that a lack of understanding about India’s concerns over cross-border terrorism will affect India-US bilateral ties.Flagging issues pertaining to each other’s sensitivities, the minister said that terrorism was of particular importance to India.“There are very few countries which have been subjected to the kind of terrorism that we have from a neighbour as part of a deliberate, conscious policy over many, many decades,” Jaishankar said, without naming Pakistan.“Now, if something which matters so deeply to us, there isn’t enough understanding or appreciation or empathy of that, I think that creates a problem too. That you know if... one of my primary concerns is not fully appreciated by my partner, then clearly there is an impact of that on the relationship,” he said, alluding to India-US ties.Jaishankar’s remarks followed US President Donald Trump’s sharing on social media a video clip of Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif’s UNGA speech where he thanked the president for his “timely intervention” to end India’s Op Sindoor. Jaishankar was speaking at the Asia Society Policy Institute where he was asked about the state of the bilateral relationship amid differences over trade and tariffs.The minister said that the trade deal both sides are finalising can improve relations, but added that the period it took to reach the understanding created bumps in the relationship.Bear in mind, India is a society of small producers, small agriculture producers, small factories. Apart from the per capita gap between India and the US, the nature of production, nature of society is very different,” he said.“A trade negotiation required a certain amount of ... patience and detailing to see it through… The expectation that it could rapidly move forward, I think, was tested against a ground reality which was much more complex,” added the minister.Jaishankar said that “today, we have reached a situation where there is more or less an understanding on the trade agreement”.India and the US had in Feb announced the finalisation of the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement. However, changes in the US tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.The two sides have since continued negotiations on their bilateral trade agreement amid the changes in the US tariff regime. Jaishankar, alluding to comments by commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal, said the issue now was what had changed on the American side and how the new Section 301 process would affect the agreement. “The 301 process is still in the works, it’s still unfolding. So the issue for us is at what point do you close out an agreement which is very, very far advanced,” Jaishankar said.“But the period that it took to reach it, that did create bumps last year for the relationship. So presumably, if that agreement is closed out, that would be one point which would contribute to a better relationship,” he said.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar: A lack of understanding about India’s concerns over cross-border terrorism will affect India-US bilateral ties. “There are very few countries which have been subjected to the kind of terrorism that we have from a neighbour as part of a deliberate, conscious policy over many, many decades,” he said.

Article Title: Pakistan airspace closed, India eyes China skies
Article Text:
Air India, which lost Rs 4,000 crore due to Pakistan airspace closure in a year, had made a presentation on the Hotan waypoint route.

NEW DELHI: India is trying to work out a “Pakistan bypass” with China for its domestic airlines as the latest closure since April 2025 has made routes between Delhi and West unviable due to longer detours amid soaring oil prices. India is in talks with China to make the Hotan route in Xinjiang available to its airlines.The Hotan plan has been in the works for months, with Air India and IndiGo doing feasibility studies. AI’s Boeing 777s, B787s and Airbus A350s can take the route. IndiGo can do so after it starts getting A350s.“We are exploring alternate airspaces and Hotan is under discussion. Diplomatic-level talks are underway. We are strongly pushing for Hotan. We are asking Indian airlines to launch more international flights from other parts of India (where western routes are not impacted by Pak airspace closure) like the south and improve connectivity from there,” aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on the sidelines of Routes Asia 2027 Tuesday.India is keen on a Pakistan bypass as international travel is growing at about 5% over the past decade, while airlines’ growth plans are hit by the neighbour’s airspace closures.To be sure, India also reciprocally closes its airspace for Pak airlines but their operations are mainly to the West.Air India, which lost Rs 4,000 crore due to Pakistan airspace closure in a year, had made a presentation on the Hotan waypoint route.Some AI wide body aircraft have additional oxygen storage, allowing them more time to step descend to 14,000 feet and then 10,000 feet in case of single engine failure or cabin de-pressurisation while flying out of the region.This is the second time in five years that Air India has found an alternate way around an airspace closure. Before Aug 2021, AI flights used the Pakistan-Afghanistan-Turkmenistan/Uzbekistan route. After Taliban took over Kabul, AI took the longer route via south Pakistan and then Iran-Turkey. In a few months, Air India found a way out by overflying the Hindu Kush.A plane gets lighter as it burns fuel, allowing it to ascend. A wide body taking off from Delhi for Europe or North America is tanked up for the non-stop journey and must overfly the Hindu Kush, where minimum altitude is 30,000 feet. The tallest mountain is 25,289-foot Terich Mir.Air India finalised the Hindu Kush route for the B787 after one-and-a-half months of simulator studies as it could fly at about 35,000 feet. For the heavier B777, it took under four months to finalise procedures for overflying Hindukush and ensure it also maintained 30,000 feet.
Article Summary: India is in talks with China to make the Hotan route in Xinjiang available to its airlines. Hotan plan has been in the works for months, with Air India and IndiGo doing feasibility studies. This is the second time in five years that Air India has found an alternate way around an airspace closure.

NEW DELHI: Three Gujarat residents who allegedly left for the US through an illegal route have gone missing after reaching Ethiopia, with their families claiming they were kidnapped and that the abductors have demanded a ransom of Rs 1 crore for their release.The three — two women and a man who are related to each other — left Gujarat on September 20 with the help of an agent from Mehsana district, who allegedly connected them with another agent in Vadodara, their relatives told reporters. Police said their whereabouts have not been ascertained since September 22.The missing persons have been identified as Rutvik Jansari of Vadsma village in Mehsana, Mamta Chavda, originally from Mehsana and now living in Ahmedabad, and Mayuri from Gandhinagar.Mamta's father, Kiritbhai Chauhan, said the family had paid around Rs 70 lakh for each person to an agent to arrange their journey to the US. After the three reached Ethiopia, they were allegedly held captive and their abductors demanded Rs 1 crore for their release, he claimed."We have already paid huge money to send them (to the US). We have nothing left and are helpless. We request the government to bring our three children back safely," Chauhan said, appealing to the authorities for help.Rutvik's grandfather Kanubhai Jansari also claimed that the kidnappers had demanded Rs 1 crore and said Rs 60 lakh had already been paid to the abductors. A local agent, Alpesh Panchal, separately told reporters that a Rs 1 crore ransom had been demanded.Police said Mamta's father lodged a missing persons complaint on Tuesday. Inspector A M Gehlot of Langhnaj police station said Mamta's husband, Chirag Kumar, had travelled to the US on a student visa around six months ago. Mamta had allegedly made several unsuccessful attempts to obtain an American visa before her family approached intermediaries to arrange her travel through an illegal route.According to the complaint, Rs 75 lakh per person had allegedly been fixed for the journey, following which Mamta, Rutvik and Mayuri left Gujarat on September 20."On September 22, Kiritbhai spoke to his daughter Mamta. After that, there has been no contact with her. A missing person's complaint was registered at the Langhnaj police station after family members failed to establish contact with the three," Gehlot said.(With inputs from PTI)
Article Summary: The three — two women and a man who are related to each other — left Gujarat on September 20 with the help of an agent. Article Title: New NCERT book says Indian kings received swords from goddesses to resist religion-driven invasions

NCERT’s new class nine social science textbook, released on Tuesday, mentions that many kings and princes received swords from goddesses such as Kali, Durga, and Bhavani to resist invasions since the seventh century.The chapter titled "Resistance and Resilience" in the book "Understanding Society India and Beyond-Part 2" outlines successive invasions of the Indian subcontinent since the seventh century."Annamaraja, ruler of Bastar is believed to have received his sword from Manikyadevi (Danteshvari) while Kumara Kampana (Vijayanagara) was believed to have used a goddess-given sword against the Sultanate forces at Madurai. Similarly, Shivaji is also traditionally believed to have obtained a sword from goddess Tulja Bhavani," the chapter reads.The chapter also describes religious traditions in warfare, with the worship of goddesses being a long-standing tradition.The first part of the textbook was released in June.According to the chapter cited by PTI, the subcontinent witnessed successive invasions since the seventh century which were driven by territorial expansion and religious motives.It also mentions how and when Indian rulers and communities resisted against Arab, Turkish, Mughal and European forces.The textbook also claims that Mughal brutality against Sikh gurus has few comparisons in history.According to NCERT chief Dinesh Saklani, Social Science learning at secondary level aims to encourage critical inquiry."Social Science learning at this (secondary) stage is expected to cultivate analytical and discursive abilities, encourage critical inquiry, promote intercultural understanding, and enable learners to participate with confidence and responsibility in civic and social life", Saklani said."It is in this spirit that Understanding Society: India and Beyond, the Grade 9 Social Science textbook for the Secondary Stage, has been conceptualised and developed," he added.

NEW DELHI: In a relief to persons with disabilities (PwD) owning cars, govt has extended the validity of exempted FASTags (free pass) from the existing one year to up to five years, depending on the degree of disability. The revised norms will come into effect from Oct 2, Gandhi Jayanti.Vehicles specially designed and built for PwDs, as well as vehicles registered under ownership type “Divyangjan”, under Motor Vehicles Act and rules are exempted from paying user fee on national highways. At present, the validity of such exempted FASTag is one year.In a communication to NHAI, road transport ministry said that under the revised procedure for exempted FASTags for PwDs with 70% to 100% disability will be valid for five years, while those with more than 40% but less than 70% disability will be valid for three years.The ministry has linked the validity of the tags to the percentage of disability recorded in a valid disability certificate, Unique Disability Identity (UDID) card or other applicable records. The tags will be renewed, thereafter, subject to continued eligibility and compliance with National Highways Fee Rules.The ministry said the revised provision was aimed at avoiding recurring procedural requirements for issuance of exempted FASTags to eligible divyangjan/ PwD vehicle owners.
Article Summary: Vehicles specially designed and built for PwDs, as well as vehicles registered under ownership type ‘Divyangjan’, under Motor Vehicles Act and rules are exempted from paying user fee on national highways. At present, the validity of such exempted FASTag is one year.

NEW DELHI: The five-day Uttar Pradesh International Trade Show (UPITS) 2026 concluded on Tuesday with the signing of 4,400 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) worth approximately Rs 6,500 crore (around USD 680 million), while potential business worth around Rs 15,500 crore was estimated from business enquiries received during the event.The fourth edition of the trade show was held at the India Expo Centre & Mart from September 25 to 29. Official figures from the Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) cited in the press release indicated that the event recorded 41,500 B2B and business meetings.Of these, 13,500 meetings took place in the Reverse Buyers-Sellers Meet (RBSM) area, while approximately 28,000 business interactions were recorded in the main exhibition area.Through these meetings, domestic and international buyers directly worked out the framework for long-term business partnerships with the state's entrepreneurs and manufacturers.A total footfall of 5,98,693 visitors and buyers was registered across the five days, comprising 1,74,990 domestic business buyers and 4,23,703 general visitors.The figures represented an increase across key business parameters compared to the 2025 edition.Total B2B meetings increased by 31.12 per cent from 31,650 in 2025 to 41,500 this year. Sessions with foreign buyers in the RBSM section rose by 123.1 per cent from 6,050 to 13,500, while meetings in the main exhibition area grew by 9.38 per cent.The number of MoUs signed rose by 12.82 per cent from 3,900 to 4,400, while their estimated value rose by 142.54 per cent from Rs 2,680 crore (USD 425 million) to Rs 6,500 crore (USD 680 million). Business enquiries also recorded a 24 per cent rise, leading to an estimated potential business increase from Rs 12,500 crore to Rs 15,500 crore.International participation expanded from a single partner country, Russia, in the previous edition to six partner nations this year, namely Russia, Austria, Japan, Singapore, Belarus, and Vietnam. Overseas delegations engaged with sectors including manufacturing, information technology, electronics, textiles, and agri-food processing.Chief minister Yogi Adityanath's ambitious "One District, One Dish (ODOC)" scheme remained the main attraction among foreign and domestic buyers throughout the event. Traditional crafts, handloom products, brass products, carpets, the leather industry and distinctive agricultural products from the state's 75 districts gained direct access to the global market.With MSMEs and local artisans receiving direct orders from international companies, the event's business character proved to be more practical and result-oriented.Overall, the event has proved to be a concrete and significant milestone towards making the state a one-trillion-dollar economy.
Article Summary: The Uttar Pradesh International Trade Show (UPITS) 2026 concluded on Tuesday. The fourth edition of the trade show was held at the India Expo Centre & Mart from September 25 to 29. The event proved to be a concrete and significant milestone towards making the state a one-trillion-dollar economy.

Article Title: FCRA bill improvement on existing law, says government
Article Text:
MPs from opposition parties and BJP clashed over provisions of the bill with two DMK MPs, A Raja and P Wilson, dubbing the bill violative of Article 300(A), which says no one will be deprived of their property save by the ­authority of law.

NEW DELHI: The vesting of assets is the single-most contentious provision in the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill but the law ministry on Tuesday said the proposal was, in fact, an improvement upon the existing law as its ­structured framework enhanced legal certainty, administrative efficiency and accountability in managing foreign-funded assets.The current law provides for vesting of assets but does not specify the nature, duration and finality of such vesting, the ministry told a joint committee of Parliament, which is examining the bill, adding that it led to an open-ended custodial arrangement and administrative difficulties in managing assets, sources said.The ministry was represented by legislative secretary Rajiv Mani at the meeting where State Bank of India, the only bank designated to receive foreign contributions at its New Delhi main branch, supported the bill’s objectives but made a host of suggestions, flagged concerns and sought more clarity, including on how to handle an organisation’s accounts and deposits when its permission to receive foreign donations ends.MPs from opposition parties and BJP clashed over provisions of the bill with two DMK MPs, A Raja and P Wilson, dubbing the bill violative of Article 300(A), which says no one will be deprived of their property save by the ­authority of law.They argued that the Supreme Court has in its rulings explained the ground on which the govt can seize properties and the FCRA bill was violative of this. BJP MP Nishikant Dubey said laws overseeing trusts and societies had ­similar provisions for ­seizure of assets.Turning to alleged misuse of foreign money for conversion, he said this allowed a person converted to a minority religion to enjoy twin quota benefits in some cases, which violated the right to equality. A team of senior SBI officials led by its chairperson C S Setty said while the bill provided for govt control of foreign contributions and ­assets in such cases, it left the detailed banking procedure to be prescribed in rules, ­sources said.SBI officers flagged a ­potential gap between the date when a registration ceased and the date the bank was informed. There is no express protection for banks acting in good faith on the instructions of the designated ­authority or the home ­ministry, they said.The bank said it supported a clear legal framework for managing foreign contributions when an organisation’s registration ended. It called for detailed rules, common procedures for banks and prompt updates on registration status before the new provisions take effect.
Article Summary: MPs from opposition parties and BJP clashed over provisions of the bill with two DMK MPs, A Raja and P Wilson, dubbing the bill violative of Article 300(A), which says no one will be deprived of their property save by the ­authority of law.

Article Text:
The emphasis on resistance comes with qualifications. Akbar’s later rule is described as relatively inclusive; Sufism receives attention, while Muslim poets Raskhan and Rahim feature among Bhakti contributors. The chapter describes a period of “both conflict and cooperation”.

NEW DELHI: NCERT’s new Class IX social science textbook puts those who resisted conquest at the centre of medieval India’s story, recounting, for instance, Queen Naiki Devi’s defeat of Muhammad Ghuri in 1178 near Mount Abu. The account also acknowledges cooperation across faiths, within a wider curricular shift connecting India’s traditions with contemporary governance and lessons in taxation, insurance and entrepreneurship.The new six-chapter Part 2 of “Understanding Society: India and Beyond” covers history, geography, political science and economics. It continues an overhaul of the earlier syllabus in which class IX history opened with the French Revolution, while economics focused on village production, poverty and food security. It follows the National Curriculum Framework for School Education 2023. Its geography chapters cover “Oceans and Life” and “Life on Earth”.“Resistance and Resilience (1000–1700 CE)” foregrounds Maharana Pratap’s resistance, Lachit Borphukan’s victory at Saraighat and Sikh opposition to Mughal persecution. Rani Abbakka Chowta’s resistance to the Portuguese extends the account beyond confrontations with Muslim rulers.It examines temple destruction and restoration, alongside the role of trade and Bhakti traditions in sustaining communities.The emphasis on resistance comes with qualifications. Akbar’s later rule is described as relatively inclusive; Sufism receives attention, while Muslim poets Raskhan and Rahim feature among Bhakti contributors. The chapter describes a period of “both conflict and cooperation”.Governance lessons invoke Mahatma Gandhi’s conception of Ram Rajya, the Sengol’s Chola associations and the ancient sources of institutional mottos. NEP 2020 is called “an excellent example” of policymaking through consultation, expert advice and public participation. The chapter also addresses misuse of public office and unequal access to services. Khelo Bharat Niti 2025 illustrates coordination between the govts, institutions and the citizens. Students are encouraged to consider their own role in governance, including providing feedback and holding public authorities accountable.Economics becomes more directly practical: students work through income-tax slabs, examine borrowing and investment risks and learn business planning. Ayushman Bharat illustrates health insurance, while entrepreneurship is linked to Viksit Bharat 2047. Lijjat Papad and hotelier Mohan Singh Oberoi provide business case studies. Exercises ask students to examine household budgets, research tax-return filing and prepare their own business plans.Paying taxes is presented as a civic responsibility.The book’s introduction explicitly records two changes to the earlier plan — “Governance and Public Policy” replaces “Authority”, while “India and the World-I” moves to Class X. NCERT says these adjustments make learning “more coherent, age-appropriate and connected”.
Article Summary: NCERT's new Class IX social science textbook puts those who resisted conquest at the centre of medieval India’s story. The account also acknowledges cooperation across faiths, within a wider curricular shift. The new six- chapter Part 2 of ‘Understanding Society: India and Beyond’ covers history, geography, political science and economics.

NEW DELHI: Observing that the right to personal liberty of the accused becomes paramount if trial is unlikely to be completed in the near future, the Supreme Court has said bail must be granted in such cases.“It is a well-settled postulate of criminal jurisprudence that pre-trial incarceration cannot masquerade as punitive detention... This court must intervene to safeguard the right to personal liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution... when a trial cannot be reasonably concluded in the near future,” a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said.The bench granted bail to ex-secretary of Rajasthan Water Supply and Sewerage Management Board Shubhanshu Dixit, who has been in custody since Feb 17, when he was arrested in a graft case.The court also granted relief to a person who was allegedly operating as a broker on behalf of the then cabinet minister of the Public Health Engineering Department, Rajasthan, Mahesh Chandra Joshi.The accused were arrested for their alleged involvement in massive financial irregularities in the execution of ‘Jal Jeevan Mission’, an ambitious joint initiative of the central and state govts intended to provide functional household tap connections for safe and adequate drinking water supply.Though the court accepted the plea of state govt that economic offences involving deep-rooted conspiracies must be viewed seriously, it granted relief to the accused.“Admittedly, the charges are yet to be framed and the trial is yet to commence for, inter alia, the following reasons: the investigation against some of the accused persons is still pending; two of the accused persons are absconding; and sanction under Section 19 of the PoC Act was granted on Sept 6 for the prosecution of six other co-accused persons who are public servants. Bearing in mind the sheer volume of evidence that must be led to prove the charges, the trial is bound to be a protracted exercise. In the conspectus of these aspects, we are of the view that it would serve no fruitful purpose to keep the appellants under further pre-trial custody. Resultantly, the present appeals succeed,” the court said.

Article Title: Can’t deny employee security clearance based on kin’s antecedents: J&K high court
Article Text:
The committee said CID’s denial of security clearance was not based on any adverse material concerning his conduct, integrity, character or antecedents but stemmed exclusively from 'the alleged antecedents of his brother and the perceived possibility of a security risk arising therefrom'

SRINAGAR: A Jammu and Kashmir high court (HC) panel Tuesday rejected a CID report against an HC staffer, observing that an employee cannot be denied security clearance solely because of his brother’s alleged antecedents.HC engaged Pampore resident Firdous Ahmad Sheikh as a daily-rated worker on April 1, 2010, and posted him at its Srinagar wing. On July 4, 2024, HC regularised his services as an orderly under the Regularization of Services of Daily Wagers in the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh Regulations, 2022.Like other appointments, Firdous’s regularisation was subject to CID verification, as is required for govt employment in J&K. On Jan 1, 2026, CID denied him security clearance, citing the “heightened adversity of his brother, Abdul Qayoom Sheikh”.The matter was placed before the Chief Justice, who referred it to the Committee for Appointment and Promotion of Officials, Officers of the High Court Staff, for consideration.The committee verified Firdous’s testimonials and found them genuine. It said CID’s denial of security clearance was not based on any adverse material concerning his conduct, integrity, character or antecedents but stemmed exclusively from “the alleged antecedents of his brother and the perceived possibility of a security risk arising therefrom”.The panel said Firdous had served the HC since 2010, and nothing adverse had been reported about his conduct, integrity or performance. “On the contrary, the record reflects that his work and conduct have remained satisfactory and that no vigilance enquiry or complaint is pending against him,” it said.Quoting J&K HC’s Feb 11, 2025 judgment in the Mohd Amir Malik v. Union of India and others case—which held that a person cannot be deprived of his legal or service rights solely on account of the conduct or antecedents of his relatives—the panel noted that liability cannot be fastened upon an individual merely on account of the alleged acts or antecedents of a close relative in the absence of any cogent material establishing the individual’s own involvement, association, complicity or misconduct.
Article Summary: HC engaged Pampore resident Firdous Ahmad Sheikh as a daily-rated worker on April 1, 2010. On Jan 1, 2026, CID denied him security clearance, citing the “heightened adversity of his brother, Abdul Qayoom Sheikh’ The matter was placed before the Chief Justice, who referred it to the Committee for Appointment and Promotion of Officials, Officers of the High Court Staff.

NEW DELHI: In the past eight months, nearly 25,000 road crash victims have been treated under PM-RAHAT, govt’s cashless scheme, and in nearly 13,000 cases, hospitals have been reimbursed for cost of treatment, a top road transport ministry official said Tuesday.Speaking at a roundtable on “Rethinking Urban Speed” organised by Road Safety Network, additional secretary in road transport ministry Mahmood Ahmed said that the scheme has helped save lives. The scheme under Motor Vehicles Act makes it mandatory for hospitals to treat road crash victims for free treatment up to Rs 1.5 lakh per victim, subject to a cap of seven days from the date of crash. Different studies suggest that 50% of lives can be saved by providing quick medical care to road crash victims.Mahmood highlighted the need to strengthen electronic enforcement of traffic rules considering that there is a tendency to break rules and deployment of manpower to detect this can never be sufficient. “Unless there is a certainty of punishment, the deterrence will never come,” he said. The official said the system would work only if violations were detected and followed through.Experts and govt officials at the workshop observed that India’s growing vehicle-safety capabilities cannot substitute for controlling speeds on urban roads, where pedestrians, two-wheeler riders and cyclists remain exposed to crash and their severity is directly linked to speedChairman of newly set up National Road Safety Board (NSRB), Nitin Gokarn, said the nature of Indian urban roads compounds the problem as different users, including pedestrians, two-wheelers, cars, trucks, and others use the same space.It’s worse in congested areas where pedestrians have no option left than walking on the main road because pedestrian facilities are absent. What adds to their risk are wrong-side driving, inadequate medians and poorly lit road infrastructure.Gokarn said at times when segregation of vulnerable road users is not possible, there are cars and bikes on roads that can reach speeds of 240 kmph and 100 kmph. This makes them vulnerable and more so when the speed is higher, he said.Experts, at the meet, shared examples such as Paris which has a maximum speed of 30 kmph or less on 89% of its urban road network; Brussels-Capital Region has 86%. They added that speed management in Indian cities needs to move beyond the setting of speed limits and focus on the interaction between road design, enforcement, local conditions and the behaviour of road users.Prof Bhargab Maitra of IIT, Kharagpur said that speed management provides an immediate opportunity to improve road safety. “Speed management is doable, implementable and workable in the short term. It is not merely about reducing speed limits; it requires the right combination of engineering, enforcement and context-based speed regulation. Aligning road design, speed limits and operating speeds, while prioritising pedestrians, cyclists and two-wheeler users, can help make our urban roads safer and more inclusive,” he said.
Article Summary: In the past eight months, nearly 25,000 road crash victims have been treated under PM-RAHAT, govt’s cashless scheme. In nearly 13,000 cases, hospitals have been reimbursed for cost of treatment, a top road transport ministry official said Tuesday.

The Madhya Pradesh cabinet has approved a 20% horizontal reservation for former Agniveers in several uniformed services and cleared schemes and projects worth more than Rs 24,500 crore, the state government said.The decisions were taken at a cabinet meeting chaired by chief minister Mohan Yadav at the state secretariat.The reservation will apply to recruitment for police constables, the Special Armed Force, jail guards, forest guards and excise constables. For excise constable posts, former Agniveers will receive 20% reservation, Home Guards 10% and ex-servicemen 5%.The cabinet approved Rs 5,329.17 crore for payment of honorariums to around 76,000 guest teachers over five years, from 2026-27 to 2030-31.It also cleared Rs 348.7 crore for school uniforms and Rs 3,245.8 crore for health centres and drug control, according to the official cited by PTI.The cabinet approved the construction of the Damoh-Katni four-lane road at a cost of Rs 4,470.30 crore and allocated Rs 3,580.22 crore to the Rural Development Fund.It also approved the continuation of major irrigation projects in Banda, Datia, Neemuch and Sagar, along with the Kanh Diversion Project in Ujjain, ahead of the Simhastha Kumbh Mela in 2028.The Rs 348.7-crore allocation for school uniforms will be transferred directly to the bank accounts of parents or students enrolled in government schools from Classes 1 to 8 during the 2026-27 academic year.The government also plans to use guest teachers to fill vacant posts in government primary, secondary, high and higher secondary schools. Madhya Pradesh currently has around 76,000 guest teachers, the official said.Under the Centre’s Agnipath scheme, Agniveers serve in the armed forces for four years, including six months of training. Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims
Article Text:
Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victims’ names redacted.The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”.The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on “archaic and stereotypical assumptions” about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.The case stems from an FIR filed by Delhi Police following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singh’s tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.Delhi Police had filed a 1,500-page charge sheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following its investigation into the allegations.The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.
Article Summary: The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”

Article Title: ‘Beating his drum away’: Congress targets PM Modi for ‘ignoring’ rising inflation in Mann Ki Baat

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi for not addressing rising inflation in his Mann Ki Baat radio address, accusing him of being “blissfully unconcerned” about the issue.The opposition party’s attack came a day after PM Modi addressed the nation in the 138th episode of Mann Ki Baat.“The brunt of inflation is no longer confined just to the kitchen, yet the Prime Minister remains blissfully unconcerned, beating his drum away. Vegetables are getting more expensive by the day, with onion prices soaring 48.27% in August. Items such as air conditioners, TVs and refrigerators are also set to become more expensive. Household savings are steadily declining, while family debt is mounting. In such a scenario, how is the common family supposed to meet its needs?” Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X.Ramesh questioned why PM Modi continues to “sermonise” in the Mann Ki Baat series instead of addressing the public’s concerns.“In his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ radio series, the Prime Minister keeps sermonising on various issues, but when will he address the country’s most pressing concern—inflation? When will he care about the public’s worries? The public is already beleaguered by rising prices, and there’s no relief coming from the government.How on earth is the average family supposed to manage its budget? How long will the middle class and the poor have their backs broken like this?” the Rajya Sabha MP asked.According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s (MoSPI) Consumer Price Index (CPI) release, retail inflation, based on the 2024=100 CPI, stood at 4.82% in August, up from 4.45% in July. Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), rose to 5.95% in August from 5.52% in July. The August figures are provisional.Official data showed that onion inflation surged from 22.54% in July to 48.27% in August. Ginger recorded inflation of 73.82%, while garlic inflation stood at 43.60%. In contrast, tomato prices fell 31.09% year-on-year, while potato prices declined 13.14%.MoSPI data showed inflation in the combined food and beverages category at 5.66% in August. Transport inflation stood at 4.60 percent, education services at 3.73%, while restaurants and accommodation services recorded inflation of 8.38%. Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services registered inflation of 15.17%.The CPI data was compiled from price information collected across 1,407 urban markets, including online markets, and 1,465 villages nationwide. MoSPI reported a 100% response rate from both rural and urban markets in August.According to MoSPI, the next CPI data, covering September, is scheduled to be released on October 12.

Article Title: Lung cancer deaths down 16% with low-dose CT screening: IARC
Article Text:
Lung cancer deaths can be reduced through low-dose CT screening, which can also help detect the disease before it reaches advanced stages in people at high risk, according to an IARC assessment.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people, while also reducing the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, an International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) working group has found.Published in The New England Journal of Medicine, the assessment found established evidence that low-dose CT reduces lung cancer mortality when used in people at high risk based mainly on age and smoking history.IARC convened a working group of 23 clinicians and scientists from 17 countries, including Dr Abhishek Shankar of All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, to assess the benefits and harms of lung cancer screening.The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history, typically at least 20 to 30 pack-years. Studies involving former smokers generally included those who had quit within the previous 10 to 15 years, with screening usually performed annually.In India, people aged 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years of smoking who are current smokers or quit within the past 15 years can contact the Indian Lung Screening Trial, led by Dr Abhishek Shankar at AIIMS, New Delhi, about screening.Dr Shankar has invited eligible people to contact him for screening under the trial.The evidence behind the finding came mainly from randomised trials. In the US National Lung Screening Trial, people screened with low-dose CT had a 16% lower relative risk of dying from lung cancer than those screened with chest X-rays at seven years. The European NELSON trial also found lower lung cancer mortality among men screened with low-dose CT at 10 years.Based on this evidence, the IARC group classified low-dose CT as Group A, indicating established evidence that it reduces lung cancer mortality and the incidence of stage III or IV disease. Chest X-rays, with or without sputum examination, were classified as Group C, as their ability to reduce lung cancer mortality could not be established.However, the review cautioned that low-dose CT screening is not meant for everyone. False-positive results ranged from 1% to 42% across studies, depending on the screening protocol. Among those with false-positive results, 5% to 32% underwent at least one invasive procedure, with complications occurring in 10% to 22% of such procedures.The review also estimated that 3% to 26% of lung cancers detected in randomised trials involving high-risk people could represent overdiagnosis, meaning cancers that might not have caused harm during the person's lifetime.The working group said effective lung cancer screening needs more than CT scanners, including systems for identifying eligible people, assessing risk, monitoring nodules, providing treatment and follow-up, along with smoking-cessation support. Organised programmes also require trained staff, quality assurance, adequate healthcare capacity and equitable access.
Article Summary: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people. It can also reduce the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, according to an IARC assessment. The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history.

Article Title: SIR on duty, just not for studies: Full academic year may be at risk
Article Text:
Their duties have expanded further following a change in the verification process for voters who could not be traced or whose records showed discrepancies.





NEW DELHI: With teachers juggling classrooms and election work for months, educators fear their continuing deployment could end up taking a toll on an entire academic year in some govt schools.What began as a time-bound exercise has stretched through crucial months of teaching, and with SIR-related work expected to continue till Dec, school heads say managing regular classes, examinations and evaluation alongside field duties is becoming increasingly difficult.“The entire academic year is getting affected,” said a govt school principal. “If teachers continue with this work till Dec and Census-related work begins after that, when the entire staff may again be involved, then when will teaching happen?”A large number of teachers serving as booth-level officers (BLOs) are balancing their regular school responsibilities with work related to Election Commission ’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR).Their duties have expanded further following a change in the verification process for voters who could not be traced or whose records showed discrepancies. BLOs will now have to visit such voters at their homes, collect the required documents and upload them for scrutiny by the electoral registration officer, rather than requiring these cases to be resolved through in-person hearings.According to the head of a school in northwest Delhi, teachers deployed for the exercise are now expected to remain engaged till Dec, although the work had initially been expected to conclude around Oct.He added that while officially the directions state that work has to be done “beyond school hours”, it was impossible to manage along with regular classes.“In my school, I have given them relaxation for half the day. They remain in school till around 11am and we schedule their periods accordingly. After that, they leave for this work,” he said. But elsewhere, he added, teachers are expected to remain in school until 1pm or 2pm before beginning field visits.“A teacher works in school till 11am, noon or even 2pm, then goes into the field and works there till 6pm or 7pm. After that, there is uploading work at night. They are doing this on Saturdays and Sundays as well,” the principal said, adding that the loss of even one teacher can be especially difficult at the senior secondary level, where a school may have only one person teaching a specialised subject.Another school head said 34 teachers from his school had earlier spent more than 40 days on full-time BLO duty. Even when teachers are asked to keep election work outside school hours, that boundary does not always hold. “They come to us at noon or 1pm and say they have to go to the field,” he said. “It is at the cost of studies.”School heads are also being drawn into the exercise. The northwest Delhi principal said 53 principals in his zone had recently been assigned SIR-related duties after a notification at the end of Sept.Meanwhile, teachers remain answerable both to their schools and to election officials. The northwest Delhi principal said some school heads who resisted relieving teachers for election work had received show-cause notices.
Article Summary: A large number of teachers serving as booth-level officers are balancing their regular school responsibilities with work related to Election Commission ’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) Their duties have expanded further following a change in the verification process for voters who could not be traced or whose records showed discrepancies.

Article Title: Delhi high court stays FSSAI order asking Red Bull to remove ‘energy drinks’ tag

NEW DELHI: Delhi HC on Tuesday stayed an order of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) that had directed Red Bull India Private Ltd to stop using the words “energy drink” on its product.Justice Amit Mahajan faulted FSSAI for not following “principles of natural justice”, noting that it passed the June 30 direction to Red Bull without giving any opportunity to the company to file a reply or give any explanation.However, the HC allowed FSSAI to take a fresh decision in the matter after following due process by issuing a show-cause notice to Red Bull and granting it an opportunity of hearing. Article Title: Delhi-Hyderabad train runs over sheep; RPF puts toll at 195, owner at 375
Article Text:
Balamoni Kistaiah, the owner of the sheep, said he had kept the flock in an enclosure nearby on Monday night.

Shepherd’s family claims Rs 40 lakh loss

Shepherd's family claims 40 lakh loss, seeks govt aid





HYDERABAD: At least 195 sheep were confirmed dead after a flock strayed onto railway tracks and was run over by the Dakshin Express near Aushapur in Medchal-Malkajgiri district in the early hours of Tuesday. The owner of the flock, however, put the death toll at 375 and said another 50 sheep were injured.The Dakshin Express, travelling from New Delhi to Hyderabad, was passing through the stretch between Bibinagar and Ghatkesar railway stations when the incident occurred at around 2.32 am, according to railway officials.Balamoni Kistaiah, the owner of the sheep, said he had kept the flock in an enclosure nearby on Monday night.According to RPF officials, the owner suspects that the sheep panicked after stray dogs barked at and chased them, causing the animals to flee towards the railway tracks.Kistaiah was asleep when the incident occurred. When he woke up, he found that the flock was missing and began searching for the animals. He later found several of them dead on the railway tracks.While Kistaiah estimated that 375 sheep had died and another 50 were injured, Railway Protection Force personnel said they had accounted for 195 deaths so far."We are probing the matter to ascertain the actual extent of loss," said Rakesh Meena, RPF inspector, Cherlapally. The RPF has registered a case.Veterinary doctors are conducting postmortem examination on the dead sheep to assess the extent of the loss, said Y Ashok Reddy, Bibinagar tahsildar. He said the govt would take a decision on compensation after the postmortem reports."A detailed PME report and findings of the inquiry will be submitted to the Medchal-Malkajgiri district collector for consideration of monetary assistance, as the family did not have insurance for the flock," Reddy said.The family has appealed to the govt for financial assistance, estimating the loss at around ₹40 lakh. "The sheep have been our livelihood for decades. We lost hundreds of animals in a matter of minutes," said Kothapally Jangaiah, a close relative of Kistaiah. Jangaiah said the family had brought around 600 sheep to the area for grazing.
Article Summary: Dakshin Express was travelling from New Delhi to Hyderabad when the incident occurred. The owner of the flock, however, put the death toll at 375 and said another 50 sheep were injured. The family has appealed to the govt for financial assistance, estimating the loss at around ₹40 lakh.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses
Article Text:
Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses

Revenue growth draws investor attention

Huge infrastructure spending

Losses add to valuation questions

Customer concentration remains a risk

Anthropic has put a massive price tag on the AI boom, backing it with an equally heavy spending plan.The AI giant is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion even as it plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.The company’s IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters, also shows just how quickly its business has grown. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments.The scale of its plans has also spilled into markets, with European technology shares rising 2.4% and the US chip index gaining 1.5%.For investors, Anthropic’s rapid expansion is a key part of the valuation story.Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar, Amsterdam, said the speed of the company’s growth stood out in the prospectus."If anything, the acceleration of the business is the biggest part of this release. Growing a big business can be difficult, but the prospectus stating that revenue grew by 12 fold in 2025 is truly remarkable."Field said the proposed valuation should be considered alongside the company’s sales."Obviously a $2 trillion valuation sounds outlandish, but when you break it down to a multiple of sales, likely to be around 18-20x, it sounds much more reasonable than the recent SpaceX IPO."Anthropic’s plans also show that the AI investment cycle is continuing to require substantial spending on infrastructure.Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB Platform, London, said the planned spending was positive for companies involved in semiconductors and AI infrastructure."This is positive for the AI trade, since it is fuelled by continued elevated levels of capex spend. The fact that Anthropic is planning on spending big on capex means that the capex cycle is not over yet. This is good news for semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies. I believe that if Anthropic had signalled a lower level of spending, this could have caused a wobble in the AI trade, since it would lead to fears about the sustainability of the AI trade as we move into Q4. "The prospectus puts rapid revenue growth alongside the large infrastructure commitments needed to support it.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, London, said Anthropic’s expectations for AI’s economic impact appeared to have supported demand for European technology stocks."It's the vision and the projections to the extent to which Anthropic believes AI will be a game changer for economies around the world that seem to have lifted demand for European tech stocks."She also raised concerns over the company’s spending while it remains loss-making."There still will be niggles of concern among some about the huge sums that are projected to be spent even though it is making a loss. But that hasn't caused a flutter of general fear because, overall, there still seems to be a pretty hefty appetite for AI focused investments."Anthropic’s losses remain another factor in the debate around its proposed valuation.Field said the losses were a concern when considered against the company’s current revenue, growth rate and size. However, he said investors had already absorbed much of the spending story."The losses certainly are a concern. Particularly given the growth rate and the size relative to current revenues. It's unlikely to deter investors, however, with the spend story having been digested for some time now."He said the scale of planned investment also reflected management’s confidence in future demand."The key takeaway for investors is the confidence in the business and the AI strategy. Yes spend is high and growing, but management obviously feel the growth rate inherent in demand is sufficiently attractive to keep spending, hence why they are coming to market and demanding a top-dollar valuation."Anthropic’s revenue growth is another area attracting attention, particularly because a significant share reportedly comes from a small number of customers.Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, London, said the company’s revenue growth had become the main focus despite its spending plans. "Massive spending would normally have investors running for the hills, but what's capturing the market's attention is Anthropic's stellar revenue growth, up 12-fold in 2025. Admittedly, AI is moving at such a rapid pace that last year’s sales achievements relate to technology that is already outdated. Article Title: RBI rate hikes ahead? BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027
Article Text:
BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) could raise interest rates by 100 basis points through the first half of 2027, according to Bank of America (BofA) Securities. The brokerage has also moved up its estimate for the first rate hike, now expecting the hike in October instead of December.BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.The new forecast is twice the size of BofA's earlier 50 basis point estimate.“Our bigger forecast shift is arguably the quantum of hikes, as we are raising our total quantum of hikes from 50bp earlier, to 100bp now,” BofA said.BofA expects the RBI to raise rates by 50 basis points in the fourth quarter of 2026 and another 50 basis points in the first half of 2027. It also expects the central bank to change its monetary policy stance in December.“The RBI will switch the stance in December to one of calibrated tightening”, the report said.So, what has changed in BofA's view? The brokerage said the domestic economy remains resilient, giving the RBI less reason to wait before raising rates.At the same time, inflation risks are becoming broader.Oil prices remained around $100-110 per barrel for most of September, BofA said. It also pointed to rising risks of fuel price increases and food-related supply pressures.Strong economic growth is another factor behind the revised outlook. BofA said the strength of the economy is reducing the need for the RBI to keep monetary conditions accommodative.Non-food credit growth stood at 17.8 per cent year-on-year in September, while investment demand is expected to remain healthy in the second quarter of FY27.Inflation pressures are also spreading, according to the report. BofA said food inflation is becoming more broad-based, while wholesale inflation is increasingly spreading to other sectors. Tradables inflation rose to 5.9 per cent in August 2026.The brokerage has also laid out a scenario in which the RBI could go beyond the 100-basis-point increase it currently expects. If real GDP growth stays around 7 per cent and headline inflation remains close to 5.5 per cent, BofA said the central bank could raise rates by more than 100 basis points.In that case, front-end rates could rise above 6.5 per cent, the brokerage said.But a sharp slowdown in growth could change the rate outlook. BofA said the RBI could deliver fewer hikes or no hike if growth falls below 7 per cent and moves towards 6 per cent on a forward-looking basis.
Article Summary: Bank of America Securities sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027. BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.

Article Title: 90% of dementia cases in TN go undiagnosed: State turns focus to early screening and care
Article Text:
About 35% of those screened had hypertension, which, says Ramani, is among the risk factors for dementia (AI Image)





CHENNAI: With more than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed, the state is looking at making the condition a “public health priority”.“Tamil Nadu has a rapidly ageing population. People over 60 make up 16% of the population in 2026, and it is projected to reach 20% in 10 years. The number of people with dementia is projected to double to 10 lakh,” says Ramani Sundaram of Dementia India Alliance (DIA), which recently organised DemCon in Chennai, a conference on the condition.DIA is a national organisation focused on dementia awareness, care, support and brain healthAt DemCon, state health minister K G Arunraj said the govt would work towards a “coordinated state plan”. “The MoU between the department of health and family welfare and DIA is an important step in this direction,” said Arun Raj. “This partnership is an expression of our shared commitment to strengthening dementia care.”The state plan will look at standardising screening, assessment, referral and treatment, as well as making diagnosis, systematic referrals and follow-up part of the existing primary healthcare infrastructure.“It’s important to create awareness as dementia care costs about Rs 3 lakh per person annually, apart from the informal cost of care provided by family members,” says Ramani. “Cognitive impairment cannot be reduced to simply asking an elderly person whether they are becoming forgetful. ”An ongoing screening programme conducted since Feb by DIA in collaboration with the state govt among 2,500 elderly people in Coimbatore, Erode and Chengalpet, found 9% had cognitive impairment.Among those screened, 30% reported neurological problems such as slowness, tremors, falls or limb weakness, while 28% had sleep disturbances. About 27% reported feeling sad, irritable, or disinterested in their usual activities, while 18% had trouble with memory, wayfinding or planning. About 12% had difficulty speaking, understanding, naming, reading or writing, and 7% said they heard voices or saw images when alone.About 35% of those screened had hypertension, which, says Ramani, is among the risk factors for dementia. “There was substance abuse in about 15% of those screened, while a large percentage – 42 – chewed tobacco. These are also among the risk factors. Up to 45% of dementia can be prevented if these are addressed. So, this is an important part of the action plan to make Tamil Nadu a dementia-aware state,” says Ramani.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu has a rapidly ageing population. People over 60 make up 16% of the population in 2026, and it is projected to reach 20% in 10 years. More than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed. The state is looking at making the condition a ‘public health priority’

Article Title: Military-grade drones worth Rs 1 crore seized at Delhi airport
Article Text:
The passengers told officials that the drones and their parts were brought from Hong Kong for a friend who owns them.





NEW DELHI: Three Indian passengers have been charged for attempting to smuggle drones and their parts worth Rs 1 crore. These passengers had arrived at IGI Airport on Sept 25 from Hong Kong via Vietnam.During Customs proceedings, the passengers were subjected to a baggage search, which resulted in the recovery of 10 autel robotics mdx-1 drones, 11 remote controllers of autel robotics mdx-1 drones, 10 adaptors, 10 USB chargers, 20 data cables, 40 remote controller joysticks and other parts. They also recovered one iPhone 18 Pro Max 512 GB.“Chartered engineer informed Customs officers that these are professional-grade drones with thermal imaging and laser range-finder and are military/defence grade UAV. They also require mandatory DGCA registration for each drone. The total market value was assessed at Rs 1 crore,” said a Customs official.The passengers told officials that the drones and their parts were brought from Hong Kong for a friend who owns them.“One passenger also stated that he intentionally smuggled these drones into India without declaration to the Customs authorities and without payment of applicable Customs duty,” said the official.
Article Summary: Three Indian passengers have been charged for attempting to smuggle drones and their parts worth Rs 1 crore. These passengers had arrived at IGI Airport on Sept 25 from Hong Kong via Vietnam.
